contexts.text: Everyone who commits actual sin, thereby induces a nature upon himself, and the evil therefrom is implanted in his children...
If thou doest not well, sin coucheth at the door () = if thou dost not will well, there is no charity, but evil.
Sin in general is meant by the devil.
He said he was a sinner. Described.
It is not meant that He took sins upon Himself.
From (the love of self) are all things called sins, etc.
Sin () = all infidelity.
Sin () = evil.
Thou hast brought on me... a great sin () = the doctrine of faith... in danger.
That those of the Spiritual Church could not be saved unless the Lord had come, is meant by, I came not to call the just, but sinners to repentance ().
If they only think... that He took away their sins...
Guilt = the blame or imputation of sin.
Guilt = all sin, which remains.
If anyone believes himself pure from sins... when he has once performed repentance... or after confession... or after the Holy Supper; if he lives a new life, this falsity can be mingled with good.
To be purified from sins through the reception and putting on of the Lord's righteousness. Signified.
What is my sin? () = that it was not of evil. Sin = evil.

How shall I do this great evil, and sin to God () = thus disjunction and no conjunction. Evil, and also sin, = disjunction and no conjunction... Evil, regarded in itself, and also sin, is nothing else than disjunction from good. Explained.
If you want to know what evil, and consequently what sin is, study to know what the love of self and the world is.

They sinned () = inverted order; for to sin = to act against Divine order. Whatever is against this, is sin... Those are against this order who are not in truth from good... Nothing else is signified by sin.

I remember my sins this day () = concerning the state of disjunction; for sins = the things which are of inverted order; thus to remember sins = to be conjoined with the things of inverted order, consequently to be disjoined from the Natural represented by Pharaoh.
Man is born into sin... Every man is born into so many hereditary evils... and hence is nothing but sin; and therefore, unless he is regenerated, he remains wholly in sin.

They believe that sins are remitted in an instant; and some that they are wiped away like dirt... For they do not know what sin is... Sins cannot be wiped away, but they are separated, or rejected to the sides... when the man is kept in good by the Lord; which cannot be done unless evil is continually cast out... AC 5398:2.

They are told that the Lord remits the sins of everyone who from his heart longs for it, but still they are not separated from the diabolical crew... They afterwards learn that to be separated from the Hells is to be separated from sins... Man is so evil that he cannot be fully delivered from even one sin to eternity; but only by the Lord's mercy, if he has received it, can he be withheld from sin.
Sin not against the child () = lest they be disjoined, namely, the external from the internal. To sin = disjunction; for all sin disjoins.
I shall sin to thee all the days () = that the good of the Church will be no longer. To sin = disjunction, thus that it will not be; for what is disjoined from anyone is no more with him. AC 5841.
As death is from no other source than sin, and sin is all that which is against Divine order, evil closes the smallest vessels...
To sin () = a turning away.
When by sin is meant evil dominant (it = Hell) as in .
Forgive the transgression of thy brethren and their sin () = supplication and repentance... Transgression = evil against truth; and sin, evil against good, which is greater. Illustrated.
Thy people have sinned () = that they have guilt in that they have done evil. To sin = to become guilty of evil...

Truth is falsified when it is said that sins are wiped and washed away... and still more when it is said that man has the power of remitting sins... and also when it is said that the Lord has derived all sins unto Himself...
I have sinned this time () = separation from truth and good; for to sin = disjunction and turning away from the Divine, thus from truth and good; consequently also separation (from them).
He added to sin () = recession still further. To sin = disjunction, recession, and separation, from truth and good.

I have sinned to Jehovah your God and to you () = confession that they have not obeyed the Divine and the truth. To sin = to do [what is] against Divine order, and to avert and separate one's self from it, and thus from good and truth; thus also not to obey the Divine and the truth; for he who does not obey, averts himself.
All disease is thence, because it is from sin.
That diseases = sins. Illustrated.
He who wants to be saved must confess his sins, and perform repentance.
Under Confess, see this reference. AC 8390.
Sins are remitted (only) by repentance of the life. Sins are continually being remitted... but the sins adhere to the man... and are not removed from him except by a life according to the precepts...
After man ... has acknowledged his sins... he must remain constant.
That ye sin not () = the conservation of spiritual life; for spiritual life is preserved by not sinning.

To sin is to do and think what is evil and false intentionally and from the will; for the things (so done) are such as go forth from the heart, and render the man unclean, consequently which destroy spiritual life in him.
Under Remit, see this reference. AC 9333:2, et seq.
Those evils are called sins which are done contrary to the goods of charity and of love. Illustrated.
Lest they make thee sin to Me () = lest evils avert the goods which are from the Lord. To sin = to avert.
Man cannot loose one sin; for sin is not loosed except by the formation of a new life...
(The doctrine) of the remission of sins. NJHD 159. TCR 611.
The sins man does are inrooted in his very life, and make it; and therefore no one is delivered from them unless he receives a new life from the Lord... by regeneration.
The signs that sins are remitted. Enumerated.
The signs that sins are not remitted. Enumerated.
Sins, when remitted, are believed to be wiped away... but they remain with the man. Their being said to be wiped away is from the appearance, when the man is withheld from them.
The bullock in the sacrifice of sin = the purification of good from evils in the external man.
The confession of sins upon the living goat = the separation and casting out in every way of evil from good. AC 9937:8.
He who alone fights for man against the Hells... is said to bear sins. Explained.
Worships representative of removal from sins. Signified, Explained.
For sins are removed through faith and love from the Lord. For in proportion as the good of love and of faith enters... sins are removed.
It is these things which expiate, that is, remove sins...

This is sin () = thus purified from evils and falsities; for sin, when it means sacrifice, = purification from evils and falsities; for, in the Original, by sin, where sacrifices are treated of, is meant sacrifice for sin, and sacrifice = purification from evils and falsities. Illustrated. AC 10122. AC 10210.
Sin by error () is sin from ignorance in which is innocence. AC 10132:10.
Thou shalt cleanse from sin upon the altar () = purification from evils in Heaven and the Church. Sin = evil; for all evil from man is called sin.
The holy things were polluted when the people sinned. Illustrated.
The blood of the expiations of sin () = the truths which are from the good of innocence. Explained.
That thou hast brought upon them so great a sin () = that that nation has averted itself from the Divine... Sin = a turning away from the Divine. AC 10504.
You have sinned a great sin () = total estrangement and turning away.
Perhaps I shall expiate for your sin () = a possibility from the Divine power with those who have so completely averted themselves.
I will visit upon them their sin () = when is the Judgment... To visit sin = to be judged and condemned.
Bearing iniquity, transgression, and sin () = the removal of evil and its falsity so that it does not appear.
Be propitious to our iniquity, and to our sin () = that their interiors, which swarm with falsities and evils, may be removed.
(References to passages on sin or evil.)
The Lord... did not take away sins, but bore them. General article.
To take away sins has a like meaning to redeeming man, and saving him. Explained.
The Lord takes away sins, that is, removes them, with those who believe in Him by living according to His precepts. Explained, Illustrated.
Everyone can see... that sins cannot be taken away from man, except by actual repentance, which consists in man seeing his sins, imploring the Lord's aid, and desisting from them...
Sin is predicated of evil; iniquity, of falsity.
(On shunning evils as sins. See Flee, Shun, and in the following references, including the references to Evil at DLife 86:2.)
The decalogue teaches what evils are sins. General article.
After some combat against these (evils)... they say in their heart that they are sins... After death (such) come into Heaven.
Those who have confirmed themselves in favour of nature... account nothing as sin; because all sin is against the Divine, which they have rejected. Their state after death.

So long as a man... thinks nothing concerning evils as sins, he is in the state (of damnation); but he comes into the second state, or that of reformation, when he begins to think that there is [such a thing as] sin; and still more when he thinks that this or that is a sin... and does not will it.
The state of regeneration... begins when man desists from evils as sins...
These things do not purify man unless he... sees his sins, acknowledges them, condemns himself on account of them, and repents by desisting from them; all as of himself...
Unless man as from himself removes sins in the external man...
They who confess themselves guilty of all sins...
a. 3. They who on account of worldly things do not think of sins. Explained.
On those who favour sins, and therefore cannot know them.
Sins with these do not appear, and therefore cannot be removed. Explained. DP 321:6. Under Evil, see this reference.
These think of God in their life; for they make evils sins against God.
Preface. 6a. Doctrine of the Reformed concerning Original Sin. Quoted. BE 10.
He that washeth us from our sins () = purities from evils, and thus reforms and regenerates. AE 30.
When these things are not known, it cannot be known what sin is; for sin draws all its delight from them.
Faith alone (causes them) not to think of any sin...

Who cannot understand that he who does not... see his sins remains in them?... If it is said that they are sins, do you not, from the delight of them, excuse them? nay, persuade yourselves... that they are not sins?... and this until you do not know what sin is. (Whereas) everyone who repents, calls sins the evils which he knows, and begins to shun them, and to feel the delight of them as undelightful; and, in the same proportion, he loves goods...
That ye be not partakers of her sins () = conjoined with her abominations. See AE 1108.
Her sins have reached unto heaven () = that their evils and falsities infest the Heavens.
That polygamy is not sin with (such). Explained. CL 349.
As the Lord says: If ye were blind, ye would not have sin; but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth ().
Under Adultery, see this reference. CL 521.
He who does not discriminate between the will and the understanding... cannot know anything about the culpability of sin.
They said: We do not know what sin is.
The Council of Trent on Original Sin.
6. It is a law of order that man should purify himself from sins by his own exertion...
The Church not in man until after sins are removed: shown by comparisons.
Mere oral confession that one is a sinner, not repentance. Explained.
To act from purpose and determination is to entirely deny that it is sin... and he who thus denies and rejects sin, considers as nothing all that is called sin.

If (such) sin from ignorance, or from some overpowering concupiscence, it is not imputed to them, because they have not proposed it to themselves, nor do they confirm it with themselves. Example(s). CL 528.
The Angels charged these things upon some as evils of sin... CL 527:end.
The sins retained in an impenitent man (and their destructive effects). Shown by comparisons.
The knowledge of sin, and the exploration of some sin in one's self, begins repentance. General article. TCR 528, General article. (Compare also TCR 535.)

A more easy kind of repentance (is to say), I think, and intend this; but as it is a sin I will not do it... Everyone can... say to another, Do not do that, because it is a sin... yet few were found able to practise this...
There is no need of an enumeration of sins before the Lord...
Still, there is no harm in enumerating one's sins before a minister...
That everything from man is sin, even when he tries to do good. Fully explained. SE 1560. SE 1561. SE 1628, Explained.

What comes into thought, but not into will, is not sin. If it enters the will, or what is like the will, and he thinks that it is a sin... and it is thus shaken off, this cannot be sin, but temptation. Whereas if anything comes into thought, and into will, so that he desires to effect it provided external bonds do not hinder: this is sin. Illustrated.

Therefore he who believes (this) is free, then, from committing sin; and whatever evil he seems to himself to commit, believing at the time that... there are evil Spirits, who were [present], and who persuaded him - the evil is not appropriated to him. (This belief, however, is possible with those only who are in the faith of charity.)
On the reasoning of some that sins are wiped away in the other life. Explained.
(Many are led by the doctrine of sudden justification to believe that they can sin with impunity.)
(On those who pray for forgiveness of their sins, and still go on committing them.)
They had never thought, This is a sin; but had abstained only for external reasons.
Men may know whether they (can be with the Societies of Heaven, or not) solely from this: whether they have thought in themselves, This is a sin...
This bishop said that there is no [such thing as] sin; that adultery is not a sin... So said many others... because the Lord has borne them...
He said that it is a sin against the neighbour; but not against God...

His having borne the sins of all = that when tempted He admitted into Himself all the Hells; for thence ascend all sins or evils... And His having taken away sins = that He subjugated the Hells, so that...
Iniquity is said of the life of falsity; sin, of the life of evil... AE 475:14.
Everyone doing sin is the servant of sin (). Sin = Hell, because from Hell.
For sins are not washed away like dirt with water; but they are washed away, that is, removed, by truths and a life according to them.
For sin and uncleanness () = the removal of evils and falsities through truths.
The gentiles, meant by publicans and sinners.
To consummate transgression, and to seal up sins () = when all are in falsities of doctrine and in evils as to life.
Iniquity = falsity; sin () = the evil of falsity.
Sinful nation () = those in evils.
Our transgressions are multiplied before Thee, and our sins answer against us () = on account of falsities from evil.
(They argue that) the evils done by a man justified by faith are not sins, but infirmities of his nature. Explained.

2. Let man learn what works are sins; and that they are especially adulteries, thefts, murders, false testimonies... also that lascivious and obscene thoughts are also adulteries; that frauds and unlawful gains are also thefts; that hatreds and revenges are also murders; and that lies and revilings are also false testimonies; and so on.
The sins from which man must desist, and which he must shun and be averse to, are especially adulteries, frauds, unlawful gains, hatreds, revenges, lies, revilings, elations of mind.
For the Lord enters, and with Him Heaven, as sins are removed.
But if he desists from doing these evils from any other cause than that they are sins... he has no conjunction with Heaven. Explained. AE 825:4.
Then, in proportion as man detests these sins, good affections enter. Enumerated.
To transfer the sins of others to Himself... is contrary to the nature of the abolition of sins; for sins are not abolished except through the repentance of life of him who has sinned...

He must then learn what evils are sins, first from the decalogue, and afterwards from the Word everywhere; and he must think that they are sins against God... Hence it is that the first of reformation is to desist from sins, to shun them, and at last to be averse to them. But (to do this) he must supplicate the Lord for aid; and he must shun and be averse to them because they are contrary to the Word... and because they are in themselves infernal. (Continued. See Flee, Shun.)
Such a man knows not what sin is.

Every man who commences spiritual life because he wants to be saved, is afraid of sins on account of the penalties of Hell; afterwards, on account of the sin itself, because it is in itself nefarious; and, finally, on account of truth and good, which he loves...
So far as anyone does not Know sins... he does not see but that he is without sins. Explained. Char 205.
So far as anyone Knows sins... he can see them in himself... Explained. Char 206.
Evils are called sins from the fact that they are contrary to the Word, and to religion.
I have heard some saying that they are sinners...
I will open the true spring of sins. Every evil is conceived of the devil as a father, and is born of atheistical faith as a mother.
